DOCUMENT: intl_water_arrears_00_prefix
LABEL:    Water arrears letter, English, number written with the 00 international prefix
INTENT:   THE WORST OF THE SIX, and the only one where the reader is actively misled rather than merely underserved. 0044 118 273 4567 has 14 digits, above the 10-11 cap, but the pattern is global so it matches the 10-digit PREFIX '0044 118 273' and the cap never sees the whole number. That value reaches contact_number and is printed on card 3. The comment on PHONE says a candidate outside the range is declined whole because 'a wrong number is a call to a stranger'; this is the case where that does not happen.
==============================================================================

DOCUMENT: intl_polish_clinic_appointment
LABEL:    Clinic appointment reminder written in Polish, number written as +48
INTENT:   THE REFUSAL. A real appointment reminder carries a date, a room, a time and a number to ring, and no patient reference, because the letter is the reference. It scores date_any_script and labelled_fields and nothing else, so it sits at 2 of the 3 structural signals and is refused outright as a non document. The phone number is the third signal it should have. Polish is deliberate: the gate's English month list accidentally matches septembrie, septiembre and septembre, so a Romance-language letter is rescued by a coincidence that Polish does not get.

DOCUMENT: intl_sole_trader_invoice
LABEL:    Sole trader invoice, English, payment link and a +44 number
INTENT:   THE Q3 FALSE POSITIVE, named in KNOWN_ENGINE_DEFECTS.md before it existed and now written down. A link, a total, no reference code and a phone number the engine cannot see, so lureShape fires on a genuine invoice from a plumber. It was drafted with a mobile first and cleared the rule for the wrong reason: the six-digit run in 07700 900412 matched REFERENCE_CODE, so the number counted as a reference. The landline avoids that artefact and shows the real behaviour.

  | Eighth instalment     £157.86       1 November 2026
  | Ninth instalment      £157.86       1 December 2026
  | Tenth instalment      £157.86       1 January 2027
  | 
  | You must pay the first instalment of £157.90 by 1 April 2026.
  | 
  | Payment methods: Direct Debit, online, by telephone, at any Post Office or
  | PayPoint using the payment slip below, or by bank transfer quoting your
  | Council Tax account number.
  | 
  | Where your Council Tax goes
  | 
  | For every £1 of the Meadowbank Borough Council share of your bill:
  | 
  | Adult social care: 34p
  | Children and family services: 21p
  | Waste collection and recycling: 12p
  | Housing and homelessness: 9p
  | Roads, parks and street cleaning: 9p
  | Libraries, leisure and culture: 6p
  | Planning and regulatory services: 5p
  | Democratic services and administration: 4p
  | 
  | Budget and spending
  | 
  | Meadowbank Borough Council has set a net budget requirement of £84.2 million
  | for the year beginning 1 April 2026, an increase of 2.9% on the previous
  | year. The council tax requirement after government grant and business rates
  | income is £31.6 million.
  | 
  | Meadowshire Police and Crime Commissioner has set a precept of £268.40 for a
  | band D dwelling, an increase of £13.00 on the previous year.
  | 
  | Meadowshire Fire and Rescue Authority has set a precept of £96.30 for a band
  | D dwelling, an increase of £2.85 on the previous year.
  | 
  | Pinfold Parish Council has set a precept of £265.60 for a band D dwelling.
  | Parish precepts are set locally and are not capped in the same way as the
  | billing authority's own charge.
  | 
  | Amounts for every band
  | 
  | Band    Proportion    Amount for the year
  | A       6/9           £1,403.24
  | B       7/9           £1,637.11
  | C       8/9           £1,870.99
  | D       9/9           £2,104.86
  | E       11/9          £2,572.61
  | F       13/9          £3,040.35
  | G       15/9          £3,508.10
  | H       18/9          £4,209.72
  | 
  | The amounts above are before any discount, exemption or reduction.
  | 
  | Empty and second homes
  | 
  | A dwelling that has been empty and substantially unfurnished for more than
  | twelve months is charged an additional premium. From 1 April 2026 the premium
  | is 100% for dwellings empty between one and five years, rising to 200% for
  | dwellings empty for more than five years. A dwelling that is nobody's sole or
  | main residence but is substantially furnished is charged the full amount with
  | no discount.
  | 
  | Flooding and other reliefs
  | 
  | If your home has been affected by flooding, or has been made uninhabitable by
  | structural work, you may be entitled to a reduction for the period it could
  | not be lived in. Please contact us with the dates involved.
  | 
  | Levies and special expenses
  | 
  | The amounts shown overleaf include the following levies charged to this
  | council by other bodies and passed on in the Council Tax:
  | 
  | Meadowshire Combined Authority transport levy: £41.20
  | Environment Agency flood defence levy: £3.86
  | Meadowbank Coroner Service: £2.14
  | 
  | Special expenses of £18.40 are charged only to dwellings in the Pinfold
  | Parish area, in respect of services provided there which are provided
  | elsewhere in the borough by the parish council.
  | 
  | Business rates and the local economy
  | 
  | Business rates collected in this area are shared between this council, the
  | combined authority and central government. They are not part of your Council
  | Tax and are not affected by anything in this notice.
  | 
  | Data protection and fraud
  | 
  | The council is the data controller for the information you give us. We use it
  | to bill and collect Council Tax, to decide entitlement to discounts,
  | exemptions and reductions, and to detect fraud and error.
  | 
  | We are required by law to take part in the National Fraud Initiative. We
  | provide data to the Cabinet Office for matching against other records held by
  | public bodies. The exercise is carried out under the Local Audit and
  | Accountability Act 2014 and does not require your consent.
  | 
  | You have the right to ask what information we hold about you, to ask us to
  | correct anything that is wrong, and to complain to the Information
  | Commissioner if you are unhappy with how we have handled your information.
  | 
  | If your circumstances change
  | 
  | You must tell us within 21 days if you move, if someone moves in or out, if
  | the property becomes empty, or if you stop being entitled to a discount or
  | exemption. If you do not tell us we may impose a penalty of £70, and a
  | further £280 if you fail to provide the information after that.
  | 
  | 
  | Meadowbank Borough Council
  | Council Tax Demand Notice 2026/2027, page 2
  | Council Tax account number: 8110 0244 71
  | 
  | Explanatory notes
  | 
  | These notes form part of your demand notice.
  | 
  | Council Tax valuation bands
  | 
  | Every dwelling is placed in one of eight bands by the Valuation Office Agency,
  | based on its open market value on 1 April 1991. Your band is shown overleaf.
  | If you think your band is wrong you may make a proposal to the Valuation
  | Office Agency. The council cannot change your band.
  | 
  | Discounts
  | 
  | If only one adult lives in a dwelling as their main home, the bill is reduced
  | by 25%. Some people are not counted when we work out how many adults live in
  | a dwelling, including full time students, apprentices, people who are
  | severely mentally impaired, and certain carers.
  | 
  | If you are receiving a discount and your circumstances change so that you are
  | no longer entitled, you must tell us within 21 days. If you do not, you may
  | have to pay a penalty.
  | 
  | Exempt dwellings
  | 
  | Some dwellings are exempt from Council Tax, including those occupied only by
  | full time students, and those left empty because the person who lived there
  | has gone into hospital or a care home.
  | 
  | Council Tax Reduction
  | 
  | If you are on a low income you may be entitled to Council Tax Reduction,
  | whether you own your home, rent, are unemployed or are working. You should
  | apply as soon as possible because a reduction cannot usually be backdated.
  | 
  | Appeals
  | 
  | You may appeal if you think you are not the person who should pay, that your
  | dwelling should be exempt, or that we have made a mistake in working out your
  | bill. Write to us first. If you are not satisfied with our reply, or we do
  | not reply within two months, you may appeal to the Valuation Tribunal.
  | 
  | Making an appeal does not allow you to stop paying. You must carry on paying
  | the instalments shown overleaf while your appeal is being considered. If your
  | appeal succeeds we will refund anything you have overpaid.
  | 
  | 
  | Meadowbank Borough Council
  | Council Tax Demand Notice 2026/2027, page 3
  | Council Tax account number: 8110 0244 71
  | 
  | What happens if you do not pay
  | 
  | If an instalment is not paid by the day it is due we will send you a reminder.
  | If you pay the amount on the reminder within seven days, your instalment
  | arrangement continues as normal.
  | 
  | If you do not pay within seven days of a reminder, you lose the right to pay
  | by instalments and the whole balance for the year becomes due immediately.
  | 
  | If the balance is still not paid we will apply to the Magistrates Court for a
  | liability order. Costs will be added to your account. A liability order
  | allows us to take money directly from your wages or from certain benefits,
  | or to instruct enforcement agents, who may charge further fees.
  | 
  | If you are having difficulty paying please contact us straight away. It is
  | much easier to agree an arrangement before a liability order is made. Free
  | and independent advice on money and debt is available from a trusted advice
  | service.
  | 
  | Your personal information
  | 
  | We use the information you give us to administer Council Tax. We may share
  | it with other departments and with other public bodies to prevent and detect
  | fraud. You have the right to ask what information we hold about you.
  | 
  | Contact us
  | 
  | Council Tax enquiries: 0114 273 4567
  | Council Tax Reduction enquiries: 0114 273 4570
  | Lines are open Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm.
  | 
  | Meadowbank Borough Council, Civic Centre, Meadowbank MB1 4RT.

LABEL:    Bilingual English and Polish Council Tax Reduction decision
INTENT:   TRACK 2. The corpus had no bilingual document of any kind, and English councils with large Polish-speaking populations issue exactly this shape.
